soundness_flags.label: estimand_functional
soundness_flags.one_line: The displayed E[Y|D_{P,x}=r] is only defined up to D-law-null radii, so its two-sided limits are not a functional as written; define it by the coarea/Hausdorff ratio (with positive denominators) or specify a continuous canonical version.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 6–7, Theorem 3(ii) and Theorem 4; pp. 9–10, Theorem 6 and following discussion
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 3(ii) gives a uniform-over-trimmed-boundary smooth-bias result for a fixed law; Theorem 6 gives an n^{-1/4} distance-only lower bound and the article states that the log^{1/4} n gap is conjectured unimprovable because its lower bound is pointwise.
The manuscript studies location-based local-polynomial BATEC estimators directly using each unit's bivariate score and includes pointwise and uniform methods.
The inspected publication is Stone's 1982 Annals paper cited for the classical nonparametric regression global-rate benchmark.
The manuscript studies minimax boundary estimation under C2-type manifold models and uses reach regularity in its geometric analysis.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the conditional-at-an-exact-distance display by an explicit coarea/Hausdorff integral ratio and state the denominator positivity needed near zero; then prove that ratio converges to the Hölder version of tau_P.

Make the logarithmic converse exhibit fully operational by specifying one common finite experiment for the multi-center packing, its pairwise KL bound, and the reduction from that experiment to the coordinatewise decision restriction.

Strengthen the empirical relevance of two-sided thickness with a verifiable sufficient-condition corollary for polygonal and smooth GIS partitions, including constants implied by an interior-cone condition and the density lower bound.

recommended_next_step: Repair the conditional-distance estimand definition, then advance the field-tier minimax program with the explicit angular-density packing obligation.
